The second harmonic is -9.4 dBc and the third -20.9 dBc here, and -16.1 and -27.6 dBc post-layout. The second is common mode, so it cancels between the two outputs (-48.9 dBc in the schematic, -54.4 dBc post-layout).

@fig-vco-pnoise shows the phase noise from PNOISE and the tuning gain from PAC. The phase noise is -101.2 dBc/Hz at 1 MHz offset. Its contributions show where it comes from: 55 % from the core (pair, varactors and coil) and 36 % from the bias of the buffer, whose input capacitance loads the tank and moves the frequency with its bias current. Below 1 MHz that bias takes over: its noise passes the 170 kHz low-pass of the bias filters, so its share grows by 40 dB to 48 dB per decade towards lower offsets, against 20 dB for the core. The tuning gain from PAC, 1.87 GHz/V at 10 MHz, agrees within about 2 % with the slope of the tuning curve of @fig-vco-tune, whose frequencies the plot script takes from the zero crossings of each tuning transient.

![Phase noise from PNOISE and tuning gain $K_\mathrm{VCO}$ from PAC (VACASK), at `vtune` = 0.75 V.](fig/vco_top/vco_top_tb_pss_vacask_pnoise_pac.svg){#fig-vco-pnoise}

![Schematic tuning curve from one transient per tuning voltage (VACASK).](fig/vco_top/vco_top_tb_tune_vacask.svg){#fig-vco-tune}

![Post-layout tuning curve from `make sim-tune-lpe`, one ngspice transient per tuning voltage at TT, 27 C.](fig/vco_top/vco_top_tb_tune_lpe.svg){#fig-vco-tune-lpe}

The schematic has no leads, so @fig-vco-tune runs about 13 % high and never reaches 20 GHz. The macro is centered on @fig-vco-tune-lpe: 20 GHz is at `vtune` = 0.75 V, and it stays inside the tuning range at every corner (@sec-rf-corners).

::: {.callout-note}
With `oscillator=1`, VACASK's `pnoise` computes the noise as for a driven circuit, so it is the total output noise, phase and amplitude noise together. Close to the carrier that is the phase noise. Below about 100 kHz the result loses accuracy, post-layout already below about 1 MHz, so read it from there up, and check it against transient noise (@sec-rf-trannoise). The [Limitations](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/macros/vco/README.md#limitations) of the README list what is known.
:::

Further traps of the testbenches, all documented in the README:

- **Symbols need `spectre_format`.** Without it, an instance drops out of the Spectre netlist without a warning (see @sec-pex).
- **VACASK is case sensitive** where ngspice is not, so `VSS` and `vss` are two nodes.
- **The PDK's VACASK model of the HV varactor** keeps an ngspice voltage term that VACASK cannot evaluate. Its coefficients are all 0, so the testbenches read a copy of the corner file from `testbenches/xschem/models/` with the term removed.
- **The ngspice transient needs `rshunt=1e12`**, because the varactor model has a node without a DC path, and the operating point otherwise takes more than a minute of gmin stepping.

## Corners {#sec-rf-corners}

```sh
make sim-corners                                    # SS, TT, FF at -40 C, 27 C, 85 C, vtune 0 V and 1.5 V
make sim-corners TB=vco_top_tb_tran_lpe             # the same with the post-layout netlist
make sim-corners TB=vco_top_tb_tran_lpe RES_CORNERS="res_typ res_wcs res_bcs" VDDS="1.35 1.5 1.65"
```

`sim-corners` netlists a transient testbench once and runs [`sim_corners.py`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/macros/vco/scripts/sim_corners.py), which writes one copy of the netlist per MOS corner, resistor corner, temperature, `VDD` and `vtune`, every combination of the lists, runs ngspice on four of them at a time, and writes a CSV table. It fails when a run does not oscillate or when a tank node passes 1.5 V on the post-layout testbench. The resistors count as much as the transistors here: `Rct` feeds the core and `Rb` sets the bias, so the weak end is the high resistor corner `res_wcs` with `VDD` at 1.35 V, and the strong end `res_bcs` with 1.65 V. @tbl-vco-corners shows the three cases from the committed post-layout table, 18 runs each.

| Resistors, `VDD` | Frequency | Center tap | `VDD` current | Highest node | Lowest output |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `res_typ`, 1.5 V | 19.05 GHz to 21.31 GHz | 0.73 V to 0.81 V | 9.6 mA to 12.1 mA | 1.31 V | -12.3 dBm |
| `res_wcs`, 1.35 V | 19.10 GHz to 21.44 GHz | 0.68 V to 0.77 V | 7.1 mA to 9.2 mA | 1.16 V | -15.6 dBm |
| `res_bcs`, 1.65 V | 19.00 GHz to 21.16 GHz | 0.79 V to 0.86 V | 12.5 mA to 15.4 mA | 1.48 V | -10.1 dBm |

: Post-layout corners: SS, TT and FF at -40 C, 27 C and 85 C, `vtune` at 0 V and 1.5 V, for each resistor corner and supply. {#tbl-vco-corners}

Every one of the 162 post-layout runs starts, the tuning range covers 20 GHz at every corner (19.00 GHz to 21.44 GHz in all), and the highest tank node reaches 1.477 V. The window is narrow at the strong end, where the highest node comes close to the 1.5 V that the thin-oxide pair may see, see [Corners](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/macros/vco/README.md#corners) in the README.

## Power-Up and Enable {#sec-rf-powerup}

A kick on the tank shows that the oscillator runs, not that it starts from a supply ramp. `vco_top_tb_powerup_lpe` simulates the post-layout macro from zero: `VDD` ramps in 10 ns, `di_en` rises at 100 ns and falls at 8.1 $\mu$s, and the run ends at 10.1 $\mu$s.

```sh
make sim-powerup                # 44 post-layout transients, hours on a compute host
make sim-view-xschem            # the plot of the nominal run, with the others
```

[`sim_powerup.py`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/macros/vco/scripts/sim_powerup.py) runs that sequence and five more: `di_en` low throughout, `di_en` tied to `VDD`, the same with a 1 ns ramp, `di_en` high before `VDD`, and `di_en` 300 ns after it, at the nominal point and at the corners closest to not starting and to the highest tank node. It measures each run period by period and fails when the tank does not start, a node passes 1.5 V, a disabled run oscillates, or the output has not settled.

![Post-layout power-up and enable at TT, 27 C (ngspice): the swing of the tank and of the output, the frequency, the current from `VDD` and the voltage of the center tap, period by period.](fig/vco_top/vco_top_tb_powerup_lpe.svg){#fig-vco-powerup}

| Sequence | Runs | Result | Tank up after | Highest node |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `VDD` first, `di_en` up at 100 ns and down at 8.1 us | 5 | 5 ok | 6.4 ns at most | 1.342 V |
| `di_en` low | 19 | 19 without oscillation, tank swing below 1 nV, at most 0.6 uA from `VDD` | | |
| `di_en` tied to `VDD`, 10 ns ramp | 5 | 5 ok | 3.6 ns at most | 1.337 V |
| `di_en` tied to `VDD`, 1 ns ramp | 5 | 5 ok | 5.3 ns at most | 1.339 V |
| `di_en` before `VDD` | 5 | 5 ok | 3.6 ns at most | 1.337 V |
| `di_en` 300 ns after `VDD` | 5 | 5 ok | 3.7 ns at most | 1.342 V |

: Post-layout power-up and enable, from `vco_top_tb_powerup_lpe_corners.csv`. {#tbl-vco-powerup}

Every run passes. With `di_en` rising at 100 ns, the tank is up after 3.8 ns at TT, 27 C, and after 6.4 ns at the slowest corner. The output takes longer: the bias filters of the buffer (170 kHz) set its current, so the output reaches 99 % of its final swing after 4.8 us at TT and 5.6 us at worst, and the frequency comes within 10 MHz of its final value after 3.6 us. When `di_en` falls, the output drops below 10 % within 3 ns, and the macro draws 9 nA from `VDD` at TT, 27 C with `di_en` low.

## Transient Noise and the Post-Layout Phase Noise {#sec-rf-trannoise}

PNOISE linearizes the circuit around one periodic solution. Transient noise does not: it adds random noise sources to an ordinary transient and reads the phase noise from the zero crossings of the result. It shares no code with PNOISE and checks it, on the schematic and on the post-layout netlist. The post-layout PSS, `vco_top_tb_pss_lpe_vacask`, runs the analyses of @sec-rf-tb-pss on the post-layout wrapper of @sec-rf-postlayout with gear integration, since with the trapezoidal rule its shooting does not converge ([VACASK#174](https://codeberg.org/arpadbuermen/VACASK/issues/174)). It needs VACASK `f29d2b0` or later ([VACASK#173](https://codeberg.org/arpadbuermen/VACASK/issues/173)).

```sh
make sim-trannoise        # the schematic, 8 seeds, against PNOISE
make sim-trannoise-lpe    # the post-layout netlist, 8 seeds
make sim-pss-lpe          # PSS, PNOISE and PAC of the post-layout netlist, about 1.5 hours
```

The benches settle the oscillation for 6 ns, store the state, and run a noisy transient of 5 $\mu$s (4 $\mu$s post-layout) from it, at a fixed step of 0.25 ps with noise from 100 kHz to 100 GHz, one VACASK process per seed. [`sim_trannoise.py`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/macros/vco/scripts/sim_trannoise.py) takes the zero crossings of the tank's differential voltage, computes the phase from the period-to-period differences, and averages the spectra of the seeds. Since every seed starts from the same state, what they share is a drift and not noise, and the script subtracts it. `make check-trannoise` tests that spectrum code on synthetic jitter with a known spectrum.

![Phase noise from transient noise (VACASK, 8 seeds) against PNOISE: the schematic and the post-layout netlist.](fig/vco_top/vco_top_tb_trannoise_vacask.svg){#fig-vco-trannoise}

| Offset | PNOISE, schematic | Transient noise, schematic | PNOISE, post-layout | Transient noise, post-layout |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 MHz | -101.2 dBc/Hz | -99.4 dBc/Hz | -101.5 dBc/Hz | -101.1 dBc/Hz |
| 3 MHz | -113.5 dBc/Hz | -112.5 dBc/Hz | -112.4 dBc/Hz | -110.9 dBc/Hz |
| 10 MHz | -124.7 dBc/Hz | -124.9 dBc/Hz | -123.3 dBc/Hz | -123.5 dBc/Hz |
| 30 MHz | -134.5 dBc/Hz | -134.9 dBc/Hz | -133.0 dBc/Hz | -133.8 dBc/Hz |
| 100 MHz | -145.1 dBc/Hz | -145.8 dBc/Hz | -143.6 dBc/Hz | -143.7 dBc/Hz |

: Phase noise from PNOISE and from transient noise. {#tbl-vco-trannoise}

`make sim-trannoise` checks PNOISE with an analysis that shares no code with it: on the schematic, transient noise over 8 seeds and PNOISE differ by -0.7 dB to +1.9 dB from 1 MHz to 100 MHz, with a scatter of the seeds of about 0.9 dB at 1 MHz. Post-layout they differ by -0.8 dB to +1.5 dB, with a scatter of 1.0 dB at 1 MHz. At 1 MHz the post-layout PNOISE is 0.3 dB below the schematic's, less than the 1.0 dB that the lower carrier alone would give.

## Post-Layout Simulation {#sec-rf-postlayout}

The post-layout testbench `vco_top_tb_tran_lpe` is the start-up transient around the wrapper [`vco_top_lpe.sch`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/macros/vco/testbenches/xschem/vco_top_lpe.sch), which puts three models together: the extraction of the macro without the coil and the varactor array (@sec-rf-verify), the EM model of the coil at the coil's feeds, and the schematic of the varactor array at the middle of its buses. The corners, the power-up, the post-layout transient noise and the post-layout PSS place the same wrapper.

```sh
make klayout-pex-leads
make sim-xschem TB=vco_top_tb_tran_lpe
```

| TT, 27 C, `vtune` = 0.75 V | Schematic | Post-layout |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Frequency | 22.51 GHz | 20.00 GHz |
| Tuning range, `vtune` 0 V to 1.5 V | 21.62 GHz to 24.01 GHz | 19.34 GHz to 21.18 GHz |
| Tank nodes | 0.10 V to 1.53 V | 0.24 V to 1.23 V |
| Output, from the peak-to-peak swing | -7.4 dBm | -10.0 dBm |
| Center tap | 0.78 V | 0.76 V |
| `VDD` current | 11.6 mA | 10.9 mA |

: Schematic against post-layout, both from the ngspice transient. {#tbl-vco-postlayout}

![Start-up transient of the post-layout netlist (ngspice).](fig/vco_top/vco_top_tb_tran_lpe.svg){#fig-vco-tran-lpe}

- **The frequency falls by 11 %**, through the capacitance of the leads and of the buffer's input, which the tank sees through the coupling capacitors.
- **The swing is smaller**, because the resistance of the leads adds to the coil's own loss: from the coil's feed 1.3 $\Omega$ to the varactors, 2.1 $\Omega$ to the pair's drains and 4.8 $\Omega$ to its gates.
- **The macro is centered on this simulation.** The varactors are sized so that 20 GHz sits in the middle of the post-layout tuning range, and `Rct` so that every post-layout corner starts and stays below 1.5 V.

The post-layout simulation changed the layout three times. The first core joined the source bar of the pair to `VSS` through a single via stack, which the extraction showed as 14.7 $\Omega$ in series with the core current. Later, with every resistance extracted, half of the corners did not start: the leads had several ohms in series with the tank, and the `VSS` strap of the macro, 2 $\mu$m of the thin Metal5, put 5.1 $\Omega$ between the pin and the pair. Via rows along the gate pads, tank lines doubled on Metal4, via stacks along the source bar and a TopMetal2 strap over the `VSS` strap fixed both, and the path from the `VSS` pin to the sources has 1.4 $\Omega$ now. The gate lines of the buffer came last: Magic reads a net that only drives gates as one node, so a port on each input (`LEADS_PROBES`) had to make the extraction keep their resistance, and two via rows along the gate pads hold it at 5.8 $\Omega$.

## Full RF Macro Flow {#sec-full-rf-flow}

```sh
make all                  # layouts, verification, deliverables and simulations, about 28 minutes
make em-model             # EM simulation of the coil, its model and the ACSP check, 35 minutes on a compute host
make sim-corners TB=vco_top_tb_tran_lpe RES_CORNERS="res_typ res_wcs res_bcs" VDDS="1.35 1.5 1.65"
make sim-tune-lpe         # post-layout tuning curve, about a minute
make sim-powerup          # power-up and enable, hours on a compute host
make sim-trannoise        # transient noise of the schematic against PNOISE, hours
make sim-trannoise-lpe    # post-layout phase noise, hours
make sim-pss-lpe          # post-layout PSS, PNOISE and PAC, about 1.5 hours
```

A new RF macro starts as a renamed copy of this one: `make macro FROM=vco NAME=<name>` in [`macros/`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/tree/main/macros/), as for the digital and the analog macro.

::: {.callout-tip}
## More Open-Source RF Designs
[SPARX](https://github.com/iic-jku/SG13CMOS_SPARX) goes further on every step of this chapter: a 160 GHz six-port receiver generated with GDSFactory, the EM simulation of multi-port passives, vector-fit models of its seven-port core, and HB, HBAC, HBNOISE and transient noise on a power detector. Its [documentation](https://iic-jku.github.io/SG13CMOS_SPARX/) walks through the flow.
:::


# Bondpad, RF Pad and Logo Implementation {#sec-ip}

The [`ip/`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/tree/main/ip/) folder holds the three custom IP cells that the top-level chip relies on: a bondpad and two logos. These IPs are generated and require zero hand drawing. Each IP ships with a Python script and Makefile targets that produce the final GDS and LEF, and run KLayout and gdscheck DRC. This makes it easy to re-spin a different bondpad size or shape, swap the logo image, or move the artwork to another metal layer without touching layout tools.

The three IP cells covered in this section are:

- [`sg13g2_ip__bondpad_70x70`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/tree/main/ip/sg13g2_ip__bondpad_70x70/), a 70 µm × 70 µm square bondpad built from IHP's `SG13_dev` KLayout PCell library,
- [`sg13g2_ip__jku`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/tree/main/ip/sg13g2_ip__jku/), the [Johannes Kepler University Linz](https://www.jku.at/) logo, generated from a PNG image,
- [`sg13g2_ip__jku_names`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/tree/main/ip/sg13g2_ip__jku_names/), a companion text block with the names of the institute, generated the same way as the JKU logo.

All three IPs follow the same folder structure (`script/`, `final/`, `verification/`) and the same Makefile conventions as the digital and analog macros (`make help`, `make all`, `make clean`, `make klayout-drc`, `make magic-drc`, `make gdscheck-drc`). The logo folders `sg13g2_ip__jku` and `sg13g2_ip__jku_names` have an additional `logo/` folder that contains the source PNG image. The folder also holds an RF pad, which the chip does not use by default, see @sec-rf-pad.

## Directory Structure

The IP design files are located in [`ip/`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/tree/main/ip/), and the relevant folders are:

| Folder                                                                                                                                                                                  | Content                                                                                          |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| [`sg13g2_ip__bondpad_70x70/script/`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/tree/main/ip/sg13g2_ip__bondpad_70x70/script/) | KLayout Python script ([`bondpad.py`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/ip/sg13g2_ip__bondpad_70x70/script/bondpad.py)) that instantiates the `SG13_dev::bondpad` PCell and writes the GDS and LEF. |
| [`sg13g2_ip__jku/logo/`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/tree/main/ip/sg13g2_ip__jku/logo/) and [`sg13g2_ip__jku_names/logo/`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/tree/main/ip/sg13g2_ip__jku_names/logo/) | Source PNG images (`jku_logo.png`, `jku_names.png`) for the two logos. |
| [`sg13g2_ip__jku/script/`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/tree/main/ip/sg13g2_ip__jku/script/) and [`sg13g2_ip__jku_names/script/`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/tree/main/ip/sg13g2_ip__jku_names/script/) | PNG-to-GDS converter ([`img2lay.py`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/ip/sg13g2_ip__jku/script/img2lay.py)) shared by both logos. |
| `final/gds/`, `final/lef/`, `final/lib/`, `final/vh/` | Build deliverables for top-level integration: GDS, LEF, Liberty, and Verilog blackbox stubs. |
| `verification/drc/` | DRC reports produced by `make klayout-drc`, `make magic-drc` and `make gdscheck-drc`. |

::: {.callout-tip}
Read the [bondpad README](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/ip/sg13g2_ip__bondpad_70x70/README.md), the [JKU logo README](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/ip/sg13g2_ip__jku/README.md), and the [JKU names README](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/ip/sg13g2_ip__jku_names/README.md) first to get familiar with the Makefile targets and parameters. Most of the commands below are also documented there.
:::

## Bondpad Generation

The bondpad is generated by the Python script [`script/bondpad.py`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/ip/sg13g2_ip__bondpad_70x70/script/bondpad.py), which runs in KLayout batch mode (`klayout -zz`). It

1. instantiates the `bondpad` PCell from IHP's `SG13_dev` library,
2. places it in a top cell named after the output file, as the static child cell `bondpad`,
3. writes the layout as a GDSII file, and
4. generates a matching LEF macro description for OpenROAD / LibreLane.

Geometry and metal stack are parameterised through three Makefile variables. The defaults match the chip's padframe and the SG13G2 PDK defaults.

| Variable       | Default  | Description                                                                                                                                  |
| -------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `DIAMETER`     | `70.0`   | Bondpad diameter / side length in µm.                                                                                                        |
| `SHAPE`        | `square` | Pad geometry. Allowed: `square`, `octagon`, `circle`.                                                                                        |
| `BOTTOM_METAL` | `3`      | Lowest metal in the pad stack: `1`=`Metal1` .. `5`=`Metal5`, `6`=`TopMetal1`. Top is fixed to `TopMetal2`. Default `3` matches `bondpad_bottomMetal` in [`sg13g2_tech.json`](https://github.com/IHP-GmbH/IHP-Open-PDK/blob/main/ihp-sg13g2/libs.tech/klayout/python/sg13g2_pycell_lib/sg13g2_tech.json). |

The available Makefile targets for the bondpad are summarised below.

| Target        | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `bondpad`     | Generate GDS and LEF via [`bondpad.py`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/ip/sg13g2_ip__bondpad_70x70/script/bondpad.py) (`make bondpad [DIAMETER=<um>] [SHAPE=<square\|octagon\|circle>] [BOTTOM_METAL=<1-6>]`). |
| `verilog`     | Generate a Verilog blackbox stub.                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `klayout-drc` | Run KLayout DRC (`make klayout-drc [CELL=<cellname>] [DRC_LEVEL=<precheck\|macro\|regular>] [DRC_JOBS=<n>]`).                                                                                                                                                 |
| `magic-drc`   | Run Magic DRC (`make magic-drc [CELL=<cellname>]`), not part of `make all`.                                                                                                                                                     |
| `gdscheck-drc` | Run gdscheck DRC (`make gdscheck-drc [CELL=<cellname>] [DRC_LEVEL=<precheck\|macro\|regular>] [GDSCHECK_SUITE=<suite>\|GDSCHECK_DECKS=<decks>] [DRC_JOBS=<n>]`). |
| `open`        | Browse this folder with `sak-open.py` and open each file in its tool (needs the VNC/X11 desktop).                                                                                                        |
| `clean`       | Remove the `final/` and `verification/drc/` output directories.                                                                                                                                         |

To execute the `clean`, `bondpad`, `verilog`, `klayout-drc`, and `gdscheck-drc` targets in sequence, run:

```sh
cd ip/sg13g2_ip__bondpad_70x70
make all
```

View the bondpad layout in KLayout with:

```sh
ke final/gds/sg13g2_ip__bondpad_70x70.gds
```

![`sg13g2_ip__bondpad_70x70` layout in KLayout.](fig/bondpad_logo/bondpad_layout.png){#fig-bondpad-layout width=60%}

The bondpad goes from `Metal3` up to `TopMetal2` by default, but the `BOTTOM_METAL` Makefile variable can be set to change the lowest metal in the stack. The pad is surrounded by the pad recognition layer `dfpad` (`41/0`).

The `bondpad` target accepts the geometry and metal-stack variables as command-line overrides. For example, to build an octagonal 80 µm bondpad from `Metal2` up to `TopMetal2`, run:

```sh
make bondpad DIAMETER=80 SHAPE=octagon BOTTOM_METAL=2
```

## RF Pad Generation {#sec-rf-pad}

A signal in the GHz range feels the load of `sg13g2_IOPadAnalog`: about 475 fF at the pad, from 144 fF of devices (ngspice, 20 GHz), 229 fF of cell metal and 100 fF of bondpad (Magic). [`sg13g2_ip__rfpad_70x70`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/tree/main/ip/sg13g2_ip__rfpad_70x70/) is one cell of 80 µm × 250 µm that takes the slot of an analog pad plus its bondpad and loads the node with about 204 fF in total, metal and ESD included, with a defined return path under the pad. Its generator [`script/rfpad.py`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/ip/sg13g2_ip__rfpad_70x70/script/rfpad.py) has no parameters, the cell is fixed:

```sh
cd ip/sg13g2_ip__rfpad_70x70
make all
ke final/gds/sg13g2_ip__rfpad_70x70.gds
```

![`sg13g2_ip__rfpad_70x70` with the die edge at the bottom: the octagonal pad over its Metal1 shield, the RF line in its corridor through the IO rails, the ESD diode pair under the core rails, and the supply clamp on both sides of the line.](fig/bondpad_logo/rfpad_layout.png){#fig-rfpad-layout width=30%}

The capacitance comes down through four layout decisions:

- **A Metal1 shield under the plate.** Metal below TopMetal2 is only a ring in the `bondpad` PCell, so the plate looks straight down into the substrate, a lossy return path. A solid Metal1 plate on `vss` turns it into a capacitor to a defined ground.
- **A corridor through the rails.** The TopMetal2 and TopMetal1 rails are cut around the RF line, 5 µm clear on either side, and `iovss` and `iovdd` cross it on Metal3 to Metal5 and Metal2. Cutting TopMetal1, the layer right under the line, is worth 6.8 fF, the 5 µm gap against the `TM2.b` minimum of 2.0 µm another 2.5 fF (Magic).
- **A teardrop exit.** TopMetal2 allows only 0°, 45° and 90°, and `Pad.fR` asks for 7 µm of unchanged metal past the pad, so the line holds 14.92 µm for 7 µm and then tapers at 45° onto 4.92 µm. Past the ESD tap it narrows to 2.0 µm, because it no longer carries the strike.
- **Small ESD devices on the core rails.** `diodevss_2kv` and `diodevdd_2kv` add 52 fF. They connect to `vss` and `vdd`, so an RC-triggered clamp between `vdd` and `vss` sits in the same cell, under the IO bands.

Two kinds of faults are invisible to the usual checks: LVS compares devices, and the rails carry none, while DRC reads two touching shapes as one polygon. A pad shorted to a rail or a floating shield therefore passes both. `rfpad.py` checks the geometry and probes the connectivity before it writes any view, and stops if a check fails. Try it: set `TM2_RAIL_GAP` in the script to `4.0` and run `make rfpad`.

KLayout reports 7 `Pad.fR_M1` markers on the cell, because the shield's 3 µm collar crosses `dfpad` and the 80 µm cell has no room for the 7 µm the recommended rule asks for. The collar is what keeps the rim field of the pad off the substrate, so `make klayout-drc` waives exactly those 7 markers and fails on any other count. gdscheck flags the same collar as 3 `Pad.fR` in its `recommended` suite and is clean otherwise, and `make klayout-lvs` matches the schematic.

The chip does not use this pad by default. Its height needs a change in the pad ring step, because the rail bands of the cell abut its neighbours only when its outer edge sits where the outer edges of the bondpads are. The [RF pad README](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/ip/sg13g2_ip__rfpad_70x70/README.md#using-the-rf-pad-on-a-chip) lists what a chip needs in its `config.yaml`, together with the capacitance budget and what the ESD diodes draw when a circuit on a higher supply lifts the pad above `vdd`.

## Logo Generation

Both logo IPs share the same Makefile targets and PNG-to-GDS converter [`script/img2lay.py`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/ip/sg13g2_ip__jku/script/img2lay.py), built on the `klayout.db` Python module. The conversion proceeds in five steps:

1. Open the source PNG (`logo/jku_logo.png` or `logo/jku_names.png`) and convert it to a binary mask using a brightness threshold (default `128`).
2. Optionally invert the mask (`--invert`) so that the dark logo regions become the foreground.
3. For each foreground pixel, draw a square of side `--pixel-size` µm on the selected metal layer.
4. Merge adjacent rectangles into larger polygons (`--merge`) to keep the GDS small and DRC-friendly.
5. Add the block-bounding rectangle on the boundary layers `prBoundary` (`189/0`) and `NoMetFiller` (`160/0`).

The Makefile derives the foreground GDS layer number (e.g. `67/0` for `Metal5`) and the LEF obstruction layer name from the same `LAYER` variable, so the artwork in the GDS and the blockage exposed to the router always stay consistent.

Both logos share the same set of Makefile variables as shown below. The `jku_names` logo uses a finer standard pixel size to ensure the readability of the smaller text elements.

| Variable      | Default (`jku` / `jku_names`) | Description                                                                                       |
| ------------- | ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `IMG_SIZE_PX` | `750` / `750`                 | Source image side length in pixels. Used to compute the scale factor automatically.               |
| `BLOCK_SIZE`  | `100`  / `100`                | Physical side length of the rendered logo in µm.                                                  |
| `PIXEL_SIZE`  | `0.50` / `0.25`               | Edge of one rendered pixel in µm. Must stay ≥ the layer's minimum width (`0.21` µm on `Metal5`).  |
| `LAYER`       | `Metal5` / `Metal5`           | Foreground metal layer. One of `Metal1`..`Metal5`, `TopMetal1`, `TopMetal2`.                      |

The image scale factor is computed automatically as `BLOCK_SIZE / (IMG_SIZE_PX * PIXEL_SIZE)`, so changing any of the three keeps the rendered block at the target physical size.

The available Makefile targets for the logos are summarised below.

| Target        | What it does                                                                                       |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `logo`        | Convert the PNG into a GDSII layout using [`img2lay.py`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/ip/sg13g2_ip__jku/script/img2lay.py). |
| `lef`         | Emit a minimal LEF macro (`CLASS BLOCK`, full-area `OBS` on `LAYER_NAME`).                         |
| `lib`         | Emit a Liberty timing stub (empty cell) so the LibreLane flow can pick the cell up.                |
| `verilog`     | Emit a Verilog blackbox stub (`module sg13g2_ip__jku;`) with no ports.                             |
| `klayout-drc` | Run KLayout DRC (same `DRC_LEVEL` selection as the bondpad).                                            |
| `magic-drc`   | Run Magic DRC, not part of `make all`.                                                                                     |
| `gdscheck-drc` | Run gdscheck DRC (same `DRC_LEVEL`, `GDSCHECK_SUITE` and `GDSCHECK_DECKS` selection as the bondpad). |
| `open`        | Browse this folder with `sak-open.py` and open each file in its tool (needs the VNC/X11 desktop).  |
| `clean`       | Remove `final/` and `verification/drc/`.                                                           |

To execute the `clean`, `logo`, `lef`, `lib`, `verilog`, `klayout-drc`, and `gdscheck-drc` targets in sequence, run:

```sh
cd ip/sg13g2_ip__jku                # or ip/sg13g2_ip__jku_names
make all
```

View the JKU logo or JKU names layout in KLayout with:

```sh
ke final/gds/sg13g2_ip__jku.gds     # or sg13g2_ip__jku_names.gds
```

::: {#fig-jku-logo-layout layout-ncol=2 fig-cap="`sg13g2_ip__jku` logo (left) and `sg13g2_ip__jku` layout in KLayout (right)."}
![`sg13g2_ip__jku` logo.](fig/bondpad_logo/jku_logo.png){width=100%}

![`sg13g2_ip__jku` layout in KLayout.](fig/bondpad_logo/jku_logo_layout.png){width=100%}
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
To replace the logo with your own artwork, drop a square PNG image into `logo/` and either rename it to `jku_logo.png` / `jku_names.png`, or override `IMG_FILE` in the Makefile. A clean black-on-white image with a few hundred pixels per side and high contrast works best.
:::

## Top-Level Assembly

For top-level assembly, the [top-level Makefile](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/Makefile) exposes two wrapper targets that descend into the IP folders and call `make all`:

```sh
make build-bondpad      # build ip/sg13g2_ip__bondpad_70x70
make build-rfpad        # build ip/sg13g2_ip__rfpad_70x70
make build-logos        # build ip/sg13g2_ip__jku and ip/sg13g2_ip__jku_names
```

All three targets are part of `make build-all` (see @sec-top), so the IP cells are refreshed automatically before the chip is hardened with LibreLane. The generated GDS, LEF, Verilog stub and Liberty files are referenced by [`flow/librelane/config.yaml`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/flow/librelane/config.yaml) when assembling the chip top-level. Furthermore, the Verilog stubs are instantiated in [`rtl/chip_top.sv`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/rtl/chip_top.sv).


# Top-Level Implementation {#sec-top}

This section covers the top-level assembly and padframe generation. The top-level files that need to be understood and modified for a new chip are:

- [`rtl/chip_top.sv`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/rtl/chip_top.sv), the padframe wrapper. It instantiates one I/O cell per pad and exposes the global `clk_PAD`, `rst_n_PAD`, `input_PAD`, `output_PAD`, `bidir_PAD`, and `analog_PAD` signals.
- [`rtl/chip_core.sv`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/rtl/chip_core.sv), the core logic. It instantiates the digital and analog macros (`counter1`, `counter2`, `inverter1`, `inverter2`, `sram_0`) and wires them together and to the I/O pads.
- [`flow/librelane/config.yaml`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/flow/librelane/config.yaml), the top-level LibreLane configuration. It defines the padframe order (`PAD_WEST`, `PAD_NORTH`, `PAD_SOUTH`, `PAD_EAST`), the chip area (`DIE_AREA`, `CORE_AREA`), the PDN core ring (`PDN_CORE_RING_VWIDTH`, `PDN_CORE_RING_HWIDTH`, `PDN_CORE_RING_VSPACING` and `PDN_CORE_RING_HSPACING`), the clock settings (`CLOCK_PORT`, `CLOCK_NET` and `CLOCK_PERIOD`), the macro list (`MACROS`), the bondpads, the logos, non-default routing rules (`NON_DEFAULT_RULES`, `DRT_ASSIGN_NDR`, and `RSZ_DONT_TOUCH_LIST`), STA corners, and references to `pdn_cfg.tcl` and `chip_top.sdc`.
- [`flow/librelane/pdn_cfg.tcl`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/flow/librelane/pdn_cfg.tcl), the Tcl script that builds the OpenROAD PDN. The bottom of the file contains the custom PDN connects for `inverter1`, `inverter2`, and `sram_0`. This is the part that has to be touched when adding new macros.
- [`flow/librelane/chip_top.sdc`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/flow/librelane/chip_top.sdc), timing constraints (clock period, input/output delays).
- Reference documentation for the chip, [specifications.md](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/doc/specifications.md), [pinout.md](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/doc/pinout.md), and [floorplan.md](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/doc/floorplan.md).

For your own chip, `make project` renames these files and every reference to them in one step (@sec-new-chip), and their content is what you then adapt.

## Planning the Chip with PREP-IC {#sec-prep-ic}

Before you edit the files below, plan the chip as a whole: which pad sits where, how far each macro is from its pads, and whether everything fits on the die. [PREP-IC](https://github.com/iic-jku/prep-ic) (Pinout, Ring and Early floorplan Planner for ICs) does that for the IHP SG13G2 and SG13CMOS5L PDKs and their IO cells, and it knows the EUROPRACTICE packages. It needs neither RTL nor a LibreLane run, and one project file holds the whole plan.

[`doc/prep-ic/chip_top.json`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/doc/prep-ic/chip_top.json) is this chip as a PREP-IC project. @fig-prep-ic-gui shows it in the GUI, and @fig-prep-ic-floorplan shows the floorplan on its own.

![This chip in the PREP-IC GUI: the pad list of each side on the left, the chip view on the right, and the stat tiles and findings below it.](fig/prep_ic/chip_top_gui.png){#fig-prep-ic-gui}

![The floorplan of this chip in PREP-IC: the pads with their package pin numbers, the macros at their `config.yaml` positions, and the flylines from the marked macro pins to their pads.](fig/prep_ic/chip_top_floorplan.png){#fig-prep-ic-floorplan width=75%}

### Installing and Starting

The IIC-OSIC-TOOLS container ships PREP-IC from tag `2026.11` on. On an older image, or on your own machine with Python 3.10 or newer, install it with pip:

```sh
pip install prep-ic
```

Then, from the top of the repository:

```sh
prep-ic doc/prep-ic/chip_top.json          # open this chip in the GUI, blocks until the window closes
prep-ic check doc/prep-ic/chip_top.json    # print the findings, exit code 1 if there are any
```

The GUI needs the container desktop. `prep-ic check` needs version 0.1.2 or newer, which `pip install --upgrade prep-ic` installs. The GUI does not follow the file on disk, so reopen a project you changed from outside.

### What It Can Do

**Pad ring and die.** The *Pads* tab has one editor per side, with one line per pad. The tag selects the IO cell:

| Line | Pad |
| --- | --- |
| `clk [in]` | digital input |
| `dout[0] [out] [4mA]` | digital output with its drive strength, `[tri]` and `[io]` alike |
| `ain [analog]` | analog pad |
| `VDD [vdd]` | core supply, `[vss]`, `[iovdd]` and `[iovss]` alike |
| `RFIN [gsg]`, `LO [gsgsg]` | an RF pad between two grounds, a differential pair with three grounds |
| empty line | a free slot of one pitch |
| `=== NAME` | a power split that cuts the ring and starts the domain `NAME` |

Tag every pad: without a tag, PREP-IC guesses the function from the name, and the guess can be wrong without a message. The PDK, the package, the pad pitch and whether the die size is fixed are in the *Settings* tab, and a die that is not fixed follows the pads.

**Macros.** In the *Macros* tab, *Add Macro...* reads the size and the pins of a macro from the `final/lef/` folder of its directory, and *Add Placeholder...* stands in for a macro that does not exist yet. Tick the pins that go off-chip and drag the macro in the *Chip* tab. A flyline then runs from each ticked pin to its pad. *Add Missing Pads* adds a pad per ticked pin without one, *Suggest Supply Pads* proposes supply pads for macros without one in reach, and *Optimize Pad Order* sorts the connected pads of each side by their macro pins.

**Checks.** The stat tiles and the warning line under the chip view report pads that do not fit, missing supply pads, a signal used twice, crossing flylines, pins without a pad, split differential pairs, a sensitive pad next to a noisy one, long analog flylines, and macros that overlap or leave the core. They are planning hints: a flyline is a straight line and not a route, and the limits are defaults you set in the *Settings* tab. A supply check only asks whether a supply pad is in reach, it knows nothing about current or ESD.

**Export.** The same plan gives the pin list, a drawing of the pad ring and the LibreLane files:

```sh
prep-ic export doc/prep-ic/chip_top.json \
    --csv pins.csv --svg padframe.svg --librelane <folder>
```

The folder receives `pad_cfg.tcl` and `padring_config.yaml` (pad positions and die area), `macros.yaml` (macro views and positions), `chip_top.sv` and `chip_core_template.sv` (the pad instances and a starting point for the core), and `bondplan_pinout.yaml` for the bonding diagram of @sec-packaging. Existing files are overwritten without asking, so do not point it at `flow/librelane/` of this chip. In the GUI, the *File* menu exports the same files.

### Reading the Plan of This Chip

- **A pad belongs to a macro pin by its name**, so the pads carry pin names such as `clock_i` and `counter_value_o[0]`, not the port names of [`doc/pinout.md`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/doc/pinout.md). When two instances tick the same pin, the pad name needs the instance as well: `inverter1_vout1` and `inverter2_vout1`, while only `inverter1` ticks `vout3`, which stays `vout3`. A pad connects to one pin only, so `clock_i` draws a line to `counter1`, although the clock also feeds `counter2` and the SRAM.
- **`sram_0` is a placeholder of the size of its LEF**, drawn dashed, because the SRAM comes from the PDK and has no macro directory.
- **`counter2` has no flylines.** PREP-IC rotates a macro but does not mirror it, and `counter2` is placed with the orientation `FS`.
- **Two findings remain:** `inverter1_vout1` sits next to `inverter2_vout2`, and the flylines of `vin2` and `inverter2_vout1` cross. Both come from the pad order of this chip and do not stop the flow. Swap `vin2` and `inverter2_vout1` in the *Pads* tab and the crossing disappears.

### From the Plan to This Flow

This chip keeps its own [`rtl/chip_top.sv`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/rtl/chip_top.sv) and the `PAD_*` lists instead of the export, because the export has no `padbare` connection: its analog pads reach the core through `padres`, behind the secondary ESD resistor, which the analog outputs of this chip avoid. It also writes no PDN and no timing constraints, those stay in [`pdn_cfg.tcl`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/flow/librelane/pdn_cfg.tcl) and [`chip_top.sdc`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/flow/librelane/chip_top.sdc). So use the plan to settle the pad order and the positions, then carry them over by hand:

| In the plan | In this repository |
| --- | --- |
| Pad order per side | `PAD_WEST`, `PAD_NORTH`, `PAD_SOUTH`, `PAD_EAST` in `config.yaml`. The GUI shows the left and right sides top to bottom, `PAD_WEST` and `PAD_EAST` list them bottom to top. |
| Pad pitch | `PAD_SPACING_MULTIPLE` in `config.yaml`, see the comment above it for the arithmetic |
| Macro positions | The `instances` of the `MACROS` block in `config.yaml`. *Export MACROS...* in the *Chip* tab shows them in that form. PREP-IC does not know the strap grid of the PDN, so check the result with `--to OpenROAD.GeneratePDN` or a full run. |
| Pad and macro tables | [`doc/pinout.md`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/doc/pinout.md) and [`doc/floorplan.md`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/doc/floorplan.md) |

## Understanding `chip_top.sv`

The padframe wrapper [`chip_top.sv`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/rtl/chip_top.sv) declares the chip's parameters and ports. The parameter block at the top of the module controls the number of pads of each type and is the place to update when the pinout changes.

```{.systemverilog filename="rtl/chip_top.sv (code snippet)"}
module chip_top #(
    // Power / ground pads for digital core / analog front-end
    parameter int unsigned NUM_VDD_PADS    = 1,
    parameter int unsigned NUM_VSS_PADS    = 1,

    // Power / ground pads for I/O
    parameter int unsigned NUM_IOVDD_PADS  = 1,
    parameter int unsigned NUM_IOVSS_PADS  = 1,

    // Signal pads
    parameter int unsigned NUM_INPUT_PADS  = 1,  // excluding clock and reset pads
    parameter int unsigned NUM_OUTPUT_PADS = 17,
    parameter int unsigned NUM_BIDIR_PADS  = 4,
    parameter int unsigned NUM_ANALOG_PADS = 4
) ( ... );
```

The remaining code does not need to be modified for a pinout change, since the `generate` blocks automatically instantiate the correct number of I/O cells based on the parameter values. One `generate` block per pad type (`g_vdd_pads`, `g_vss_pads`, `g_iovdd_pads`, `g_iovss_pads`, `g_inputs`, `g_outputs`, `g_bidirs`, `g_analogs`) instantiates the matching IHP I/O cell, plus single instances for the clock and reset pads. An example code snippet of the input pad generation with a `generate` block is shown below. The `input_PAD` signals are exposed as ports of the `chip_top` module and are connected to the pads of the I/O cell, while the `input_PAD2CORE` signals are connected to the internal core logic in `chip_core.sv`. The same structure, or a very similar one, applies to the other pad types.

::: {.callout-note}
Normally, only the parameter counts need to be edited in `chip_top.sv`. Only multi-clock and multi-reset chips would require modifications to the clock and reset pad generation, since the current template supports only one clock and one reset pad.
:::

```{.systemverilog filename="rtl/chip_top.sv (code snippet)"}
generate
    for (genvar i = 0; i < NUM_INPUT_PADS; i++) begin : g_inputs
        sg13g2_IOPadIn input_pad (
            `ifdef USE_POWER_PINS
            .iovdd (IOVDD),
            .iovss (IOVSS),
            .vdd   (VDD),
            .vss   (VSS),
            `endif
            .p2c   (input_PAD2CORE[i]),
            .pad   (input_PAD[i])
        );
    end
endgenerate
```

::: {.callout-note}
The `sg13g2_IOPadAnalog` cell exposes two internal core-side nodes per analog pad:

- `padres`: path through the pad's **secondary** ESD resistor
- `padbare`: **direct** path to the pad metal (only primary ESD diodes)

In this template, `inverter2` uses both paths:

- `vin1`/`vin2` are connected to `analog_PADRES[0:1]` (resistor-protected input path)
- `vout1`/`vout2` are driven onto `analog_PADBARE[2:3]` (direct output path to avoid extra RC)

Inside `chip_core.sv`, these nets appear as the corresponding lowercase core signals `analog_padres[*]` and `analog_padbare[*]`.

```{.systemverilog filename="rtl/chip_top.sv (code snippet)"}
generate
    for (genvar i = 0; i < NUM_ANALOG_PADS; i++) begin : g_analogs
        (* keep *)
        sg13g2_IOPadAnalog analog_pad (
            `ifdef USE_POWER_PINS
            .iovdd   (IOVDD),
            .iovss   (IOVSS),
            .vdd     (VDD),
            .vss     (VSS),
            `endif
            .pad     (analog_PAD[i]),
            .padres  (analog_PADRES[i]),
            .padbare (analog_PADBARE[i])
        );
    end
endgenerate
```
:::

## Understanding `chip_core.sv`

The core [`chip_core.sv`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/rtl/chip_core.sv) is where the macros are instantiated and wired to the chip's I/O pads. The `enable` signal is mapped to `input_PAD[0]`, the two `counter_top` instances share the clock and reset, the two `inverter_top` instances are wired up (one digital, one analog), and the SRAM output is XOR-reduced to a single bit on `output_PAD[16]`. The input and output assignments at the top and bottom of the file correspond to the bit-to-role mapping documented in [pinout.md](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/doc/pinout.md). For improved clarity, every assignment is written on a separate line. Advanced designers can also use bus notation for more compact code.

```{.systemverilog filename="rtl/chip_core.sv (code snippet)"}
// ======================================================
// Input Assignments
// ======================================================
logic enable;
assign enable = input_in[0];

// Inverter 1
wire inv1_din1 = bidir_in[0];
wire inv1_din2 = bidir_in[1];
wire inv1_din3 = bidir_in[2];
wire inv1_din4 = bidir_in[3];

// Inverter 2
wire inv2_vin1 = analog_padres[0];
wire inv2_vin2 = analog_padres[1];
// ======================================================
```

```{.systemverilog filename="rtl/chip_core.sv (code snippet)"}
// ======================================================
// Output Assignments
// ======================================================
// Digital outputs
// Counter 1
assign output_out[0]  = counter1_value[0];
assign output_out[1]  = counter1_value[1];
assign output_out[2]  = counter1_value[2];
assign output_out[3]  = counter1_value[3];

// Counter 2
assign output_out[4]  = counter2_value[0];
assign output_out[5]  = counter2_value[1];
assign output_out[6]  = counter2_value[2];
assign output_out[7]  = counter2_value[3];
assign output_out[8]  = counter2_value[4];
assign output_out[9]  = counter2_value[5];
assign output_out[10] = counter2_value[6];
assign output_out[11] = counter2_value[7];

// Inverter 1
assign output_out[12] = inv1_dout1;
assign output_out[13] = inv1_dout2;
assign output_out[14] = inv1_dout3;
assign output_out[15] = inv1_dout4;

// SRAM
// Reduce the 32-bit SRAM output to a single bit by computing the parity.
// output_out[16] = 1 when an odd number of bits in sram_0_out are 1.
// output_out[16] = 0 when an even number of bits in sram_0_out are 1.
assign output_out[16] = ^sram_0_out;

// Digital bidirectionals (output side)
// Bidir output enable: drive when `enable` is high (counter visible),
// float as input when low (so external stimuli can drive inverter1).
assign bidir_out[0] = counter1_value[4];
assign bidir_oe[0]  = enable;

assign bidir_out[1] = counter1_value[5];
assign bidir_oe[1]  = enable;

assign bidir_out[2] = counter1_value[6];
assign bidir_oe[2]  = enable;

assign bidir_out[3] = counter1_value[7];
assign bidir_oe[3]  = enable;

// Analog outputs
assign analog_padbare[2] = inv2_vout1;
assign analog_padbare[3] = inv2_vout2;
// ======================================================
```

## Understanding `config.yaml`

The top-level LibreLane configuration [`config.yaml`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/flow/librelane/config.yaml) covers the following sections and references `pdn_cfg.tcl` and `chip_top.sdc`.

1. **Padframe generation.** `PAD_WEST`, `PAD_NORTH`, `PAD_SOUTH`, and `PAD_EAST`, in the order documented in [`doc/pinout.md`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/doc/pinout.md).
2. **PDN core ring.** `PDN_CORE_RING`, `PDN_CORE_RING_VWIDTH`, `PDN_CORE_RING_HWIDTH`, `PDN_CORE_RING_VSPACING`, and `PDN_CORE_RING_HSPACING`.
3. **Clock settings.** `CLOCK_PORT`, `CLOCK_NET`, and `CLOCK_PERIOD`.
4. **STA corners.**
   - `nom_fast_1p32V_m40C`
   - `nom_fast_1p65V_m40C`
   - `nom_slow_1p08V_125C`
   - `nom_slow_1p35V_125C`
   - `nom_typ_1p20V_25C`
   - `nom_typ_1p50V_25C`
5. **Non-default routing rules.** `NON_DEFAULT_RULES`, `DRT_ASSIGN_NDR`, and `RSZ_DONT_TOUCH_LIST`.
6. **Macro, bondpad, and logo placement.** `MACROS` with per-macro files and placement (`location`, `orientation`), plus top-level bondpad and logo placement settings, together with chip area and placement constraints (`DIE_AREA`, `CORE_AREA`, `FP_SIZING`, `PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT`).

::: {.callout-note}
The `NON_DEFAULT_RULES` section defines a dedicated routing rule for the analog traces of `inverter2` (`PADRES` and `PADBARE`). In this template, `NDR_analog` sets a wider wire width and larger spacing for the selected metals and vias, which helps reduce coupling and preserve analog signal quality.

The `DRT_ASSIGN_NDR` section applies this rule during detailed routing by matching net names with regular expressions (`^.*PADRES.*$` and `^.*PADBARE.*$`). The `RSZ_DONT_TOUCH_LIST` then protects the same analog nets from resizing, buffering, or other optimization steps, so the routed analog paths remain unchanged.
:::

## Understanding `pdn_cfg.tcl`

[`pdn_cfg.tcl`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/flow/librelane/pdn_cfg.tcl) is the OpenROAD callback that builds the power-distribution network (PDN). Most of the file follows the standard structure provided by LibreLane and OpenLane.

For macro changes, the bottom of the file is the relevant part. It defines per-instance PDN grids and macro connections. The current chip provides the following.

- A default macro grid (`TopMetal2` to `TopMetal1`) used by the two counters.
- A custom grid for `inverter1` and `inverter2` (`TopMetal2` to `TopMetal1` and `TopMetal2` to `Metal5`, because each inverter macro has its own internal `Metal5` / `TopMetal1` ring).
- A custom grid for `sram_0` (`Metal5` stripes bridged to `Metal4` and `TopMetal1`, because the SRAM exposes its supplies on `Metal4` and `Metal5`).

When new macros are added, the matching `define_pdn_grid` plus `add_pdn_connect` block at the bottom must be extended (or the default grid is used if the macro layers line up with the top-level grid). The custom grid for the inverters is shown below as an example. The comments explain the reasoning behind the layer choices and the connection structure.

```{.tcl filename="flow/librelane/pdn_cfg.tcl (code snippet)"}
# Custom connect for the inverter macros (inverter1, inverter2).
# The top-level power ring is on TM1 (horizontal) and TM2 (vertical).
# Each inverter has its own power ring on M5 (horizontal) and TM1 (vertical),
# so the connection between the top-level power ring and the inverter power rings crosses cleanly.
# Note: within an inverter's power ring no top-level TM1 or TM2 power rails are routed.
define_pdn_grid \
    -macro \
    -instances "i_chip_core.inverter1 i_chip_core.inverter2" \
    -name inverter_top \
    -starts_with POWER \
    -halo "$::env(PDN_HORIZONTAL_HALO) $::env(PDN_VERTICAL_HALO)"

add_pdn_connect \
    -grid inverter_top \
    -layers "$::env(PDN_VERTICAL_LAYER) $::env(PDN_HORIZONTAL_LAYER)"

add_pdn_connect \
    -grid inverter_top \
    -layers "$::env(PDN_VERTICAL_LAYER) Metal5"
```

## Top-Level Simulation

The same RTL and gate-level cocotb flow as in @sec-digital is available at top level.

```sh
make sim-rtl-cocotb
make sim-gl-cocotb
make sim-view-cocotb                                # use GTKWave as waveform viewer
make sim-view-cocotb WAVEFORM_VIEWER=surfer         # use Surfer as waveform viewer
```

The cocotb testbench at top level is [`testbenches/cocotb/chip_top_tb.py`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/testbenches/cocotb/chip_top_tb.py), and it covers the global enable, reset, counters, and bidir behaviour documented in [`doc/specifications.md`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/doc/specifications.md). The result is shown in @fig-chip-top-cocotb-gtkwave.

![`chip_top` cocotb waveform in GTKWave.](fig/chip_top/chip_top_cocotb_gtkwave.png){#fig-chip-top-cocotb-gtkwave}

For mixed-signal simulation, the [`testbenches/xschem/chip_top_tb_tran.sch`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/testbenches/xschem/chip_top_tb_tran.sch) testbench can be opened in Xschem for interactive simulation, the same way as for the counter or the inverter, and is shown in @fig-chip-top-tb-tran-schematic.

```sh
cd testbenches/xschem
xschem chip_top_tb_tran.sch
```

![Xschem top-level mixed-signal testbench `chip_top_tb_tran`.](fig/chip_top/chip_top_tb_tran_schematic.svg){#fig-chip-top-tb-tran-schematic}

Again, the simulation and plotting can be run non-interactively from the command line with the following targets.

```sh
make sim-gl-xschem
make sim-view-xschem SCRIPT=plot_chip_top
```

`sim-gl-xschem` runs in batch mode: it netlists the testbench with `xschem netlist` and then calls `ngspice -b` directly, so `make` blocks until the run finishes and sees its exit status. The testbench is selected with `TB=<testbench_name>` (default: `<CELL>_tb_tran`). Since the run is headless, the `plot` commands in the testbench's `.control` block are a no-op. The testbench exports its results with `wrdata` to [`testbenches/xschem/plot_simulations/data/`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/tree/main/testbenches/xschem/plot_simulations/data), from where `sim-view-xschem` plots them with Matplotlib.

::: {.callout-note}
The top-level Xschem testbench converges, but it may take a long time depending on the hardware used. `make sim-gl-xschem` is part of `sim-all`, so a full `make sim-all` includes it. For this tutorial, the simulation data is already available in the repository in [`testbenches/xschem/plot_simulations/data/chip_top_tb_tran.txt`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/testbenches/xschem/plot_simulations/data/chip_top_tb_tran.txt), so `make sim-view-xschem SCRIPT=plot_chip_top` can be run without running the simulation first.
:::

The following plots show the results of the top-level transient simulation. The first plot shows the analog inverter response, while the other three plots show the digital outputs of the two counters, the digital inverter, and the bidirs.

![Plotted simulation result of `chip_top_tb_tran`: analog inverter 2 response.](fig/chip_top/chip_top_tb_tran_analog_inv_sim.svg){#fig-chip-top-tb-tran-analog-inv-sim width=75%}

![Plotted simulation result of `chip_top_tb_tran`: digital inverter 1 outputs.](fig/chip_top/chip_top_tb_tran_digital1_sim.svg){#fig-chip-top-tb-tran-digital1-sim}

![Plotted simulation result of `chip_top_tb_tran`: digital counter 2 outputs.](fig/chip_top/chip_top_tb_tran_digital2_sim.svg){#fig-chip-top-tb-tran-digital2-sim}

![Plotted simulation result of `chip_top_tb_tran`: digital counter 1 / inverter 1 bidirs.](fig/chip_top/chip_top_tb_tran_digital3_sim.svg){#fig-chip-top-tb-tran-digital3-sim}

When the testbench is opened in Xschem, the schematic of `chip_top` can be inspected with the shortcuts **`e`** / **`Ctrl + e`**, and the symbol can be shown with **`i`** / **`Ctrl + e`** as explained in @sec-analog. The symbol and schematic are shown in @fig-chip-top-symbol and @fig-chip-top-schematic, respectively. The schematic shows the connections between the padframe and the core macros, while the symbol shows the pinout of the chip. The SRAM is not included in the schematic, since IHP does not ship a SPICE model or an Xschem symbol for the `RM_IHPSG13_1P_1024x32_c2_bm_bist` macro.

![Xschem symbol of `chip_top`, showing the pinout of the chip.](fig/chip_top/chip_top_symbol.svg){#fig-chip-top-symbol width=60%}
