## Building the Chip

When the floorplan and pinout are planned and configured, the chip can be built from scratch with the following command.

```sh
make build-all
```

This runs the steps in order, `init-submodules`, `build-bondpad`, `build-rfpad`, `build-logos`, `build-macros`, and `build-top`. It is the right starting point on a fresh machine after cloning the repository and entering the IIC-OSIC-TOOLS container.

To re-run only the top-level flow (for example after a change in [`config.yaml`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/flow/librelane/config.yaml) or [`chip_core.sv`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/rtl/chip_core.sv)), without rebuilding the bondpad, logos, or macros, run the following command.

```sh
make build-top
```

Internally, `build-top` runs `librelane-nodrc`, `copy-reports`, `copy-gds`, `copy-netlist`, `copy-render`, `add-logo-fill`, and
`render-gds`. The final GDS is written to [`layout/chip_top_logo_fill.gds.gz`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/layout/chip_top_logo_fill.gds.gz).

The renders generated by `sak-render.py`, which runs during the `render-gds` step, are located in [`render/img/`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/tree/main/render/img/). The verification reports (Yosys, antenna, STA, IR-drop, LVS, manufacturability) from the top-level LibreLane flow can be found in [`verification/reports/`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/tree/main/verification/reports/). The netlists are located in [`netlist/`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/tree/main/netlist/).

::: {.callout-note}
Note that currently the LibreLane flow streams out the top-level GDS `layout/chip_top.gds.gz` without the logos and the fill structures. To add the chip logo (PNG → GDS) and the fill structures on top of the LibreLane output, run:

```sh
make add-logo-fill
```

This calls `scripts/add_logo_fill.sh` with `TOP` and writes `layout/chip_top_logo_fill.gds.gz`. This step is already called by `make build-top`. In the future, it is planned to replace this script and Makefile target with a custom LibreLane step.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
The difference between `chip_top.gds.gz` and `chip_top_logo_fill.gds.gz` is that the former is the raw top-level layout without any logos or filler cells, while the latter includes the logos and filler cells added for manufacturability and cosmetic purposes. For visual debugging in KLayout, it is recommended to use `chip_top.gds.gz` to avoid the visual clutter of the logos and filler, while for DRC and LVS, `chip_top_logo_fill.gds.gz` should be used since it is the actual layout that will be taped out.
:::

## Viewing the Chip

After a successful build, the chip can be opened with KLayout.

```sh
ke layout/chip_top.gds.gz             # Chip layout without logos and filler
ke layout/chip_top_logo_fill.gds.gz   # Chip layout with logos and filler
```

![`chip_top_logo_fill` layout in KLayout ("all" layers).](fig/chip_top/chip_top_black.png){#fig-chip-top-layout width=75%}

![`chip_top_logo_fill` layout in KLayout with only `TopMetal2` selected.](fig/chip_top/chip_top_black_TM2.png){#fig-chip-top-layout-tm2 width=75%}

## Top-Level Verification

DRC, LVS, and PEX are also available for the full chip.

### DRC

The following DRC targets are available for the top-level.

```sh
make magic-drc CELL=chip_top              # Magic DRC on the bare chip
make magic-drc CELL=chip_top_logo_fill    # Magic DRC including logo + filler
make klayout-drc-minimum                  # fast pre-check KLayout DRC on chip_top_logo_fill.gds.gz
make klayout-drc-regular                  # full KLayout DRC on chip_top_logo_fill.gds.gz (slower)
make klayout-drc-regular DRC_JOBS=16      # the same on a server with 16 KLayout processes
make gdscheck-drc-minimum                 # gdscheck precheck suite on chip_top_logo_fill.gds.gz
make gdscheck-drc-regular                 # gdscheck main suite on chip_top_logo_fill.gds.gz
```

`klayout-drc-minimum` is a quick pre-check on the final top-level layout including the logo and the fill structures. `klayout-drc-regular` does the full check, but takes longer, and KLayout is the sign-off deck. `DRC_JOBS` raises the number of KLayout processes above the default of 4, which pays off for the full chip on a server with enough RAM (about 0.5 GiB per process plus the layout). `magic-drc` and the `gdscheck-drc` targets add a second and a third opinion with their own rule decks. On this chip both report violations in IHP's own cells that the KLayout deck passes: Magic in the IO pads and the SRAM macro, which it reads hierarchically, and both Magic and gdscheck 0.2.0 at the nBuLay ring of the inverter's guard ring. `make all` runs `klayout-drc-regular` and `gdscheck-drc-regular`, stops on a violation, and leaves `magic-drc` out, so it stops at gdscheck until the fix is in the container.

### LVS

The following LVS targets are available for the top-level.

```sh
make klayout-lvs                          # top-level KLayout LVS
make magic-lvs                            # top-level Magic + Netgen LVS
```

::: {.callout-warning}
The top-level LVS is currently under construction. The flow is in place, but some issues and limitations in the ihp-sg13g2 PDK must be fixed before it can run successfully.
:::

### PEX

The following PEX target is available for the top-level.

```sh
make magic-pex                            # only chip_top (without logo and filler), default EXT_MODE=1
make magic-pex EXT_MODE=3 THRESHOLD=5000 MINRES=500 MINDELAY=2   # full-RC with custom extresist settings
```

For full-RC extraction (`EXT_MODE=3`), `magic-pex` also exposes the `sak-pex.sh` `extresist` tuning parameters `THRESHOLD` (`-t`, default `10000` mOhm), `MINRES` (`-r`, default `1000` mOhm) and `MINDELAY` (`-y`, default `1` ps; `0` = gate by resistance). They are ignored in `EXT_MODE=1`/`2`.

As in the macros, `magic-pex` starts by running `make symbol-pex`, which rebuilds [`schematic/xschem/chip_top_pex.sym`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/schematic/xschem/chip_top_pex.sym) from `chip_top.sym` with `type=subcircuit` changed into `type=primitive`, so the PEX symbol always matches the current chip symbol.

::: {.callout-warning}
At the top level, PEX is only run on `chip_top` (without logo and filler), and the default `EXT_MODE=1` (C-decoupled) is used to keep the runtime manageable. However, the extracted netlist [`chip_top_magic_pex_1.spice`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/netlist/pex/chip_top_magic_pex_1.spice) is still huge (~75 MB, ~566k lines), and the post-layout simulation must be run on a powerful server.
:::

## Packaging {#sec-packaging}

The die is packaged in a QFN-32 (5 × 5 mm) open-molded plastic package ([OmPP](https://www.qptechnologies.com/products/ompp/)) from the [EUROPRACTICE ASIC packaging](https://europractice-ic.com/services/packaging/asic-packaging/) offering. The package matches the padframe exactly: all 32 bondpads (8 per side, see @sec-top) are wired one-to-one to the 32 package leads (8 per side). Bonding is done with 25 µm gold wire, the longest wire measures 1.70 mm, and the cover is glued on after bonding.

The bonding diagram below is generated fully automatically with `make bondplan` from the final chip GDS ([`layout/chip_top_logo_fill.gds.gz`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/layout/chip_top_logo_fill.gds.gz)) and the EUROPRACTICE package library [`EP_PACKAGES_08022018.gds`](https://europractice-ic.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/EP_PACKAGES_08022018.gds_.gz). The flow extracts the die bondpads together with their names, places the die in the package cavity, draws the bondwires, fills in the title block, and checks wire lengths, crossings, spacing, lead skew, and the clearance around the sensitive analog wires. The [pinout](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/packaging/config.yaml) and all flow settings are kept in a single configuration file, so the diagram never goes out of sync with the chip. Details are documented in the [packaging README](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/tree/main/packaging).

```sh
make bondplan                        # uses the default VERSION (1.0.0)
make bondplan VERSION=2.1.0          # stamp another version on the sheet
```

The `VERSION` variable is passed to the flow and printed in the title block (`DIE: CHIP_TOP - V.1.0.0`), so the version number is maintained in the Makefile only. The outputs are the bondplan GDS (`packaging/layout/chip_top_bondplan.gds`), the bond report with summary and bond table ([`packaging/result.md`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/packaging/result.md)), and the bonding diagram images (`packaging/render/chip_top_bondplan_{white,black}.{png,svg}`).

![Automatically generated bonding diagram of the ihp-sg13g2 AMS template chip in a QFN-32 package.](fig/chip_top/chip_top_bondplan_white.png){#fig-chip-top-bondplan width=70%}

::: {.callout-tip}
Check the flow log and [`packaging/result.md`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/packaging/result.md) after every run. Unbonded named pads and NC package pins are reported explicitly, so a forgotten connection in the `PINOUT` table is immediately visible. Warnings are raised for bondwires that are too long (`BONDWIRE_MAX_LENGTH`), cross each other, come too close to each other, land skewed on their lead (`BONDWIRE_MAX_SKEW`), or violate the guard clearance of sensitive wires (`GUARDED_PINS` / `GUARD_SPACING`).
:::

## Full Flow at Once

The comprehensive simulation, build, and DRC pass for the complete chip is run with the following command.

```sh
make all
```

This calls `build-all` first, then the regular KLayout and gdscheck DRC of `chip_top_logo_fill`, which stops the flow on a violation (see the DRC section above), then `sim-all` (RTL and gate-level cocotb plus the gate-level Xschem run), and finally `bondplan`. The simulations therefore run on the netlists that this build has just produced. Depending on the hardware used, `make all` can take a while.

## Releasing for Tapeout

When the chip is clean, the `release` target copies the GDS, the netlists, and the renders into a versioned folder for tapeout submission.

```sh
make release VERSION=2.1.0
```

The artifacts are written to [`release/v.2.1.0/`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/tree/main/release/) (`gds/`, `netlist/{schematic,layout,pnl,spice}/`, `img/`).

::: {.callout-important}
Run `make all` before `make release`. The release target only copies files, it does not rebuild or re-verify the chip.
:::


# Start Your Own Chip {#sec-new-chip}

The template is meant to become your own chip. Work through this tutorial on the template as it is, then start your chip from a copy of it: create your own repository with the green "Use this template" button on GitHub (or fork or copy the repository) and name it `ihp-sg13g2-<name>` after the chip, clone it, and enter the IIC-OSIC-TOOLS container. In the top-level folder of the clone, one target turns the copy into a new chip with its own name:

```sh
make project NAME=<name> DRY_RUN=1   # list the changes, touch nothing
make project NAME=<name>             # start the chip <name>
```

`NAME` is a lowercase letter followed by lowercase letters, digits or underscores, for example `mychip`. It must not be the name of a macro or an IP: with `NAME=counter`, the chip top `counter_top` would be the same cell as the top cell of the counter macro. The target needs no PDK.

::: {.callout-tip}
With the repository named `ihp-sg13g2-<name>`, for example `ihp-sg13g2-mychip`, `git clone` gives its folder the same name, and `make project` writes that name into the directory tree of the README. If your clone has another name, rename it before `make project`: rename the repository on GitHub (Settings > General, the old URLs redirect), point `origin` at the new URL with `git remote set-url origin <URL>`, close VS Code and every terminal in the folder, and rename the folder from its parent folder. `make project` lists the same steps when the folder name differs.
:::

## What `make project` Does

1. **It checks before it changes anything.** It refuses to run in a git tree with uncommitted changes, so that `git reset --hard && git clean -fd` can undo the run completely, and in a checkout whose `origin` is still the template repository. `FORCE=1` skips both checks. Every change is planned first, so a refused run, for example because of a name that is already in use, leaves the tree untouched.
2. **It deletes the outputs of the template chip** with `make clean`: the GDS in `layout/`, the netlists, the renders, the reports, the simulation results and the bondplan. They carry the old name and come from a build of the template chip. The macros and IPs keep their committed views, so the new chip builds without rebuilding them.
3. **It removes what only makes sense in the template**: this tutorial (`tutorial/`) and the workflow that publishes it, `doc/ihp-structure-proposals/`, `CITATION.cff`, the content of `release/`, and every block between `template-only` markers in the README, `AGENTS.md`, the `Makefile` and the configuration files. Figures that a remaining file still shows move to `doc/fig/`, and `ToDo.md` starts empty.
4. **It renames the chip.** `chip_top`, `chip_core` and `chip_logo` become `<name>_top`, `<name>_core` and `<name>_logo`, in file names and in file contents (see @tbl-new-chip-names). `TOP` in the `Makefile` follows, and with it every target that takes the name from `TOP`, including the logo and fill step and the bondplan.
5. **It gives the README a new header** that records the template version it started from, and deletes itself: `scripts/new_project.py` and the `project` target are gone afterwards.
6. **It checks the result.** No old name, no link into a deleted path and no `template-only` marker may be left, and `reuse lint` has to pass when it is installed. The report at the end lists what is left for you.

| Template                                    | After `make project NAME=mychip`                |
| ------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `TOP = chip_top` in the `Makefile`          | `TOP = mychip_top`                              |
| `DESIGN_NAME: chip_top` in `config.yaml`    | `DESIGN_NAME: mychip_top`                       |
| `rtl/chip_top.sv`, `rtl/chip_core.sv`       | `rtl/mychip_top.sv`, `rtl/mychip_core.sv`       |
| `flow/librelane/chip_top.sdc`               | `flow/librelane/mychip_top.sdc`                 |
| `schematic/xschem/chip_top.sch`, `.sym`     | `schematic/xschem/mychip_top.sch`, `.sym`       |
| cocotb `chip_top_tb.py`                     | `mychip_top_tb.py`                              |
| Xschem `chip_top_tb_tran.sch`               | `mychip_top_tb_tran.sch`                        |
| the instance `i_chip_core`                  | `i_mychip_core`                                 |
| `flow/logo/chip_logo_mono.png`              | `flow/logo/mychip_logo_mono.png`                |
| `layout/chip_top_logo_fill.gds.gz`          | `layout/mychip_top_logo_fill.gds.gz`, written by the first build |

: Names in the template and after `make project NAME=mychip`. {#tbl-new-chip-names}

## After `make project`

Review the result, commit it, and build the new chip:

```sh
git status             # undo: git reset --hard && git clean -fd
git add -A
git commit -m "started <name> from ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template"
make init-submodules   # the logo and fill step needs flow/artistic
make build-top         # or make all, which also fetches it
```

The first build writes the layout, the netlists, the renders and the reports under the new name (see @sec-top). Then make the chip your own:

- **Your own blocks.** In `macros/`, start a digital or an analog macro as a renamed copy of an example (see @sec-digital, @sec-analog and @sec-exercise3):

  ```sh
  make macro FROM=counter NAME=<macro>    # digital macro
  make macro FROM=inverter NAME=<macro>   # analog macro
  ```

  The [macros README](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/macros/README.md#register-the-macro-at-the-chip-top-level) lists every place where a new macro is registered at the chip top-level. Remove the example macros once your own ones replace them.
- **Floorplan, pinout and package.** Adapt the die area, the pad ring and the macro placements in `flow/librelane/config.yaml` (see @sec-top), the `PINOUT` map in `packaging/config.yaml` (see @sec-packaging), and the chip documentation in `doc/`. @sec-exercise4 and @sec-exercise5 walk through exactly these changes.
- **Regression.** The `regression` target, which the nightly workflow runs, tests the counter and inverter macros. Point it at your own macros once the examples are gone.

::: {.callout-important}
The logos stay, and they put the template's identity on the die. Replace them before a tapeout, @sec-ip shows how the logo IPs are generated from PNG images:

- [`ip/sg13g2_ip__jku_names/`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/tree/main/ip/sg13g2_ip__jku_names/) draws the names of the template authors.
- `flow/logo/<name>_logo_mono.png` draws the "AMS CHIP" artwork on TopMetal2 (see @fig-chip-top-layout-tm2).
- [`ip/sg13g2_ip__jku/`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/tree/main/ip/sg13g2_ip__jku/) draws the JKU logo, replace it where it does not apply.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
`make project` deletes this tutorial from the new chip, but it stays available online. The template's [top-level README](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/README.md#start-a-new-chip-from-this-template) describes the target as well.
:::


# Additional Exercises {#sec-exercises}

The following exercises repeat the corresponding sections of this tutorial with modifications to the design.

## Exercise 1: From 8-bit Up-Counter to 16-bit Down-Counter {#sec-exercise1}

Repeat @sec-digital for a 16-bit synchronous down-counter that wraps from 0 back to $2^{16} - 1 = 65535$. The recommended steps are:

1. Update the RTL ([`counter.sv`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/macros/counter/rtl/counter.sv), [`counter_top.sv`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/macros/counter/rtl/counter_top.sv), [`constants.sv`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/macros/counter/rtl/constants.sv)). Change the bitwidth and turn the increment block into a decrement, with wrap-around from 0 to `CTR_MAX`.
2. Update the testbenches in [`testbenches/verilog/`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/tree/main/macros/counter/testbenches/verilog/), [`testbenches/cocotb/`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/tree/main/macros/counter/testbenches/cocotb/), and [`testbenches/xschem/`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/tree/main/macros/counter/testbenches/xschem/) to cover the new behaviour. Adjust the bus width in the waveform view files (`*.gtkw`, `*.surf.ron`) as well.
3. Run `make sim-all` to validate the new RTL.
4. Re-run the LibreLane flow with `make build-top`. Check the timing reports. A 16-bit counter at 50 MHz must still pass timing constraints. Then run `make lec`, which proves the new netlist equivalent to the new RTL, now in 16 partitions (see @sec-lec).
5. Update the bus range of the output pin in the Xschem symbol ([`counter_top.sym`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/tree/main/macros/counter/schematic/xschem/)), and re-run the gate-level Xschem simulation. The XSPICE model itself is regenerated automatically by `make build-top` (or manually with `make generate-xspice`), and the PEX symbol `counter_top_pex.sym` together with the extracted netlist by `make magic-pex`. Forgetting this step no longer costs you a debugging session: `make symbol-check` runs inside `generate-xspice` and names the eight ports the symbol is now missing. Run `make symbol-gl FORCE=1` in a scratch copy of the macro if you would rather read the widened pin off a fresh scaffold than edit the range by hand.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Bonus for advanced designers

Replace the binary counter with a 16-bit Gray counter (only one bit toggles per transition). Keep only the Gray register, and `make lec` proves the design in seconds. With a binary register next to the Gray output, `make lec` fails on a correct netlist, with some partitions running into `LEC_TIMEOUT`, so `make all` stops there (see @sec-lec).
:::

## Exercise 2: Self-Biased Single-Ended Inverter Amplifier {#sec-exercise2}

Repeat @sec-analog with a self-biased single-ended inverter amplifier by adding a feedback resistor $R_\mathrm{f}$ between the output and the input of the inverter. As discussed in @sec-cace, the bare CMOS inverter has poor PVT robustness because nothing pins the gate bias to $V_\mathrm{DD}/2$. A feedback resistor closes a DC loop that forces the operating point to the high-gain crossover ($V_\mathrm{in} \approx V_\mathrm{out} \approx V_\mathrm{DD}/2$) regardless of process corner, which also linearises the small-signal transfer characteristic and turns the inverter into a usable single-ended amplifier. The disadvantage of this technique is the reduced input resistance, which equals $R_\mathrm{in} \approx 1 / (g_\mathrm{m,NMOS} + g_\mathrm{m,PMOS})$. The recommended steps are:

1. Open the inverter schematic ([`inverter.sch`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/macros/inverter/schematic/xschem/inverter.sch)) in Xschem and add a resistor between the `vin` and `vout` nets of the inverter. Use the `rhigh.sym` device from the `sg13g2_pr` PDK library, the high-sheet poly resistor. Keep `spiceprefix=X` and connect its `body` terminal to `VSS`. The symbol computes the value from the geometry: with a sheet resistance of $1360\,\mathrm{\Omega/sq}$ this is roughly $2.7\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$ per $\mathrm{\mu m}$ of length at $W = 0.5\,\mathrm{\mu m}$, so keep $W$ at $0.5\,\mathrm{\mu m}$ and set the value with $L$ (the `b` parameter folds a long resistor into segments). Start with a value of $R_\mathrm{f} = 1\,\mathrm{M\Omega}$ and adjust as needed. What can you observe?
2. Re-run the schematic-level testbenches from @sec-analog and observe the change in behaviour. First, always carefully think about what the expected behaviour would be before running the simulations, and then check if the results match your expectations. Note that the ac open-loop testbench drives `vin` directly with a voltage source, which overrides the self-biasing. To observe it, also try removing the dc bias from the input (for example by coupling the source through a large capacitor) and let the feedback set the operating point.
3. Re-run the full schematic-level simulation suite with `make sim-all` to refresh the plotted results in [`fig/inverter_top/`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/tree/main/tutorial/fig/inverter_top).
4. Re-run the CACE flow with `make sim-cace` and compare the new process and mismatch plots against @fig-inverter-cace-aol and @fig-inverter-cace-fcu. The spread of $A_\mathrm{ol}$ across corners should be visibly narrower than the open-loop reference.
5. [Optional] Sweep $R_\mathrm{f}$ in the CACE characterisation YAML ([`inverter.yaml`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/macros/inverter/verification/cace/inverter.yaml)) to study the circuit behaviour across a range of feedback resistor values.
6. [Optional] Once the schematic results are convincing, propagate the resistor to the layout in [`layout/`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/tree/main/macros/inverter/layout/) with the `rhigh` PCell, using the same $W$ and $L$ as in the schematic and dummy resistors of minimum length above and below it, and re-run the verification chain (`make klayout-verify`, `make magic-verify`) plus `make build-top`. Compare the post-layout gain and bandwidth against the schematic level as in @sec-postlayout.

::: {.callout-tip}
Choose $R_\mathrm{f}$ carefully. Too small, and the loop loads the amplifier output and degrades the closed-loop gain. Too large, and the time constant with the input parasitic capacitance dominates, so the amplifier loses gain at the low end of the signal band. A value in the $1$–$10\,\mathrm{M\Omega}$ range is a sensible starting point for this inverter sizing.
:::

## Exercise 3: Three-Stage Ring Oscillator with Output Buffer {#sec-exercise3}

Repeat @sec-analog for a three-stage ring oscillator with an output buffer, derived from the existing quad inverter. The recommended steps are:

1. Start the new macro as a renamed copy of the [inverter](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/tree/main/macros/inverter/) with `make macro FROM=inverter NAME=ringosc` in `macros/`. The target renames the files, the cells inside the GDS files and every reference, see the [macros README](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/macros/README.md) for what it does and what is left.
2. Update the schematic in Xschem. Connect three inverters in a ring, and tap the output of the last stage through a buffer. The fourth inverter of the quad inverter can naturally be used as the buffer.
3. Update the symbol of the macro ([`schematic/xschem/inverter_top.sym`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/macros/inverter/schematic/xschem/inverter_top.sym)) to expose a single output net, instead of `vin1..vin4` and `vout1..vout4`. The PEX symbol `inverter_top_pex.sym` is rebuilt from it by `make symbol-pex`, which the PEX targets run automatically.
4. Update the transient testbench ([`testbenches/xschem/inverter_top_tb_tran.sch`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/macros/inverter/testbenches/xschem/inverter_top_tb_tran.sch)) to measure the oscillation frequency. Remove the input source. Since the delay per stage is small, simulate a few hundred nanoseconds with a fine step, and measure the period between two consecutive rising crossings of $V_\mathrm{cm}$ on the output net:

   ```spice
   meas tran t_rise1 when v(vout)=Vcm rise=1
   meas tran t_rise2 when v(vout)=Vcm rise=2
   let T_osc = t_rise2 - t_rise1
   let f_osc = 1/T_osc
   print f_osc
   ```

   `Vcm` is visible inside the `.control` block only through a `.csparam Vcm=Vcm` line next to `.param Vcm=VDD/2`, as the dc testbench shows (see @sec-tb-ac). The expected relation is $f_\mathrm{osc} = 1/(2 \cdot N \cdot t_\mathrm{d})$ with $N = 3$ stages and $t_\mathrm{d}$ the effective stage delay. An ideal simulation can rest on the metastable point where all stages sit at $V_\mathrm{cm}$, so if the ring does not start, kick it with an initial condition on one ring node, for example `.ic v(osc)=0`. Delete testbenches that are no longer relevant.
5. Resize the unit inverter and watch the frequency. Vary `w`, `l`, and the finger count `ng` of $M_1$ and $M_2$ in the unit cell schematic (`ringosc.sch`), and re-run the transient simulation for each variant. Predict the outcome before you simulate, and use @sec-tradeoffs as your guide.
6. [Optional] Adapt the CACE [`inverter.yaml`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/macros/inverter/verification/cace/inverter.yaml) to characterise the oscillation frequency across PVT.
7. Update the layout in KLayout. The existing `inverter_top.klay.gds` can be used as a starting point, but the internal routing has to be modified to form the ring and the buffer stage. After editing, export a clean `ringosc_top.gds`. Keep the box on the `prBoundary` layer (`189/0`) and resize it with the macro, otherwise the top-level flow cannot place it. `make check-boundary` verifies this.
8. Re-run the verification chain, `make klayout-verify`, `make magic-verify`, and `make build-top`. Then compare the post-layout oscillation frequency against the schematic level as in @sec-postlayout. The parasitics add delay per stage, so the frequency drops.

## Exercise 4: Update Pinout and Floorplan of the Top-Level {#sec-exercise4}

Building on @sec-exercise1 and @sec-exercise3, swap `inverter2` for the ring oscillator, delete `counter2`, and connect the now 16-bit `counter1` to the freed-up south-side pads. Try the new pad order and the macro positions in PREP-IC first (@sec-prep-ic). The recommended steps are:

1. Replace `inverter2` with the ring oscillator macro in [`chip_core.sv`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/rtl/chip_core.sv).
2. Replace three of the four analog pads with VSS pads, and connect the ring oscillator's output to the fourth analog pad.
3. Delete `counter2` and rewire all eight south-side pads to the new 16-bit `counter1` values.
4. Update the parameters of [`chip_top.sv`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/rtl/chip_top.sv) so that `NUM_OUTPUT_PADS`, `NUM_BIDIR_PADS`, `NUM_ANALOG_PADS`, and `NUM_VSS_PADS` match the new pin count (see @sec-top).
5. Update the macro instantiation and wiring in [`chip_core.sv`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/rtl/chip_core.sv).
6. Update the placement coordinates in the `MACROS` block of [`config.yaml`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/flow/librelane/config.yaml). Keep the [`doc/floorplan.md`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/doc/floorplan.md) constraints in mind, namely stay in the core, no overlaps, and respect the `Metal3` grid for inverter-like macros.
7. Update the PAD lists (`PAD_WEST`, `PAD_NORTH`, `PAD_SOUTH`, `PAD_EAST`) in [`config.yaml`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/flow/librelane/config.yaml) to match the new pinout.
8. Update [`pdn_cfg.tcl`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/flow/librelane/pdn_cfg.tcl) so that the new macros are covered by the correct PDN grid (default for digital, `inverter_top`-style for analog).
9. Rebuild the chip from scratch with `make build-all`, then verify with `make klayout-drc-regular` and `make gdscheck-drc-regular`.

## Exercise 5: Update the Bondplan Configuration {#sec-exercise5}

Building on @sec-exercise4, update the bondplan configuration in [`packaging/config.yaml`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/packaging/config.yaml) so that the packaged chip matches the new pinout (ring oscillator instead of `inverter2`, 16-bit `counter1`, no `counter2`, three additional VSS pads). The recommended steps are:

1. Rebuild the final GDS of the modified chip (`make build-all` from @sec-exercise4), since the bondplan flow reads the die pads and their names directly from [`layout/chip_top_logo_fill.gds.gz`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/layout/chip_top_logo_fill.gds.gz).
2. Update the `PINOUT` table in [`packaging/config.yaml`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/packaging/config.yaml): the south-side pads now carry `counter1_value[15:8]`, three of the four east-side analog pads became VSS pads, and the fourth carries the ring-oscillator output. Keep the geometric order in mind (pins 1-8 left top→bottom, 9-16 bottom left→right, 17-24 right bottom→top, 25-32 top right→left) so that the bondwires do not cross.
3. Connect the freed-up VSS pads as downbonds to the exposed pad by adding an `EPAD` list (e.g. `EPAD: ["VSS", "VSS", "VSS"]`) and marking their former leads as NC (`~`). The exposed pad of the QFN-32 is the package ground, and the die is attached with conductive epoxy, so ground downbonds are shorter and lower-inductance than wires to leads.
4. Re-run `make bondplan` and read the flow log and [`packaging/result.md`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/blob/main/packaging/result.md) carefully: only the deliberately unbonded pads may appear as *unbonded named pads* (plus the seal-ring artifact), and there must be no wire-length, crossing, spacing, lead-skew, or guard-clearance warnings.
5. Inspect the generated bonding diagram in [`packaging/render/`](https://github.com/iic-jku/ihp-sg13g2-ams-chip-template/tree/main/packaging/render/) and the bondplan GDS in KLayout (`ke packaging/layout/chip_top_bondplan.gds`). The title block of the A4 drawing sheet (die size, pad pitch, wire count, maximum wire length) is refilled automatically on every run.
6. [Optional] Experiment with the die placement: rotate the die with `DIE_PLACEMENT.orientation` (e.g. `E`) or move it off-center with `DIE_PLACEMENT.location`, re-run the flow, and observe how the wire-length, spacing, and skew checks react. Restore a placement where all checks pass.

## Exercise 6: Re-Harden the Counter with Another Standard Cell Library {#sec-exercise6}

Repeat the hardening of @sec-digital on another library and measure what it changes. The counter uses IHP LV by default, now re-harden it with IHP HV or ETH LV, keeping the RTL, the die, the constraints and `SYNTH_STRATEGY`. What differences can you see in area, speed, and power? The recommended steps are:

1. Run `make librelane` in `macros/counter/` on the unchanged configuration and keep the run folder `flow/librelane/runs/<run>/` as the reference.
2. Switch the library as described in @sec-hardening-libraries. Stay with `make librelane`, since `make build-top` stops at `copy-reports` on another library.
3. Run `make librelane` and confirm that the run finishes with 0 DRC, LVS and antenna errors (`final/metrics.csv`: `magic__drc_error__count`, `klayout__drc_error__count`, `design__lvs_error__count`, `antenna__violating__nets`).
4. **Area.** Compare the `Chip area` line in `*-yosys-synthesis/reports/stat.rpt` and, after place and route, `design__instance__area__stdcell` and `design__instance__utilization` in `final/metrics.csv`. Which cells does Yosys choose for the flip-flops, and why does IHP LV need a `sg13g2_tiehi` per bit? For ETH LV, subtract `design__instance__area__class:tap_cell`. For IHP HV, compare `design__core__area`: the core margins scale with the site, so the taller rows lose core area to the fixed die.
5. **Speed.** Read `timing__setup__ws` in `final/metrics.csv`, then shorten `CLOCK_PERIOD` step by step (for example 5, 3, 2.5, 2, 1.8 and 1.6 ns) with `make librelane-nodrc` until `timing__setup__ws` turns negative, and compare the shortest period that closes. The flow stops with `Setup violations found` at a violating period. Note in which corner each library is slowest: the corners of IHP LV and ETH LV end at 1.08 V, those of IHP HV at 3.0 V.
6. **Power.** Read `*-openroad-stapostpnr/nom_typ_1p20V_25C/power.rpt` for IHP LV and ETH LV, and `nom_typ_3p30V_25C/power.rpt` for IHP HV. `power__total` in `final/metrics.csv` is the value of the last entry of `STA_CORNERS`, which is 1.5 V for IHP LV and 1.2 V for ETH LV, so it does not compare the two. The report of IHP HV shows 0 W of internal and switching power, because its Liberty has no dynamic power data. Why does the leakage of ETH LV come out larger than that of IHP LV, although its logic is smaller? Count the decap cells in `final/nl/counter_top.nl.v` and look up their `cell_leakage_power` in the Liberty files.
7. Restore the macro with `git restore .` in `macros/counter/` and delete `tracks_ez130.info`.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Bonus for advanced designers

The clock tree of IHP LV uses `sg13g2_buf_16` as root buffer, far more than eight flip-flops need. Set `CTS_ROOT_BUFFER` and `CTS_CLK_BUFFERS` to smaller cells in both libraries, for example `sg13g2_buf_4` and `BUFX12`, and repeat the power comparison. Then measure the supply current at transistor level, the only way to get a dynamic power number for IHP HV: `make copy-final` and `make magic-pex EXT_MODE=2` write `netlist/pex/counter_top_magic_pex_2.spice`. Include it in an ngspice deck with the nominal supply, 6 fF on each output and a 50 MHz clock, and average `i(vdd)` over 16 counting cycles with `meas tran`. A run takes 15 to 45 minutes, so it is not part of the routine flow.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Reference results

These are the results for the 200 µm × 100 µm die, `SYNTH_STRATEGY: DELAY 4` and the configurations of @sec-hardening-libraries in image tag `2026.10`, with the typical corner at 1.2 V for IHP LV and ETH LV and at 3.3 V for IHP HV.

| | IHP LV | IHP HV | ETH LV |
|---|---|---|---|
| Synthesised cell area (`stat.rpt`) | 742 µm² | 2293 µm² | 401 µm² |
| Standard cell area after place and route | 1285 µm² | 2910 µm² | 1184 µm², 748 µm² without tap cells |
| Core area and rows | 12802 µm², 18 | 8061 µm², 6 | 13395 µm², 21 |
| Utilisation | 10.0 % | 36.1 % | 8.8 % |
| Flip-flops | `sg13g2_dfrbpq_1` + `sg13g2_tiehi` | `sg13g2_hv_dfrbpq_1` + `sg13g2_hv_tiehi` | `DFFQX1` |
| Worst setup slack at 20 ns | 13.44 ns | 13.75 ns | 14.50 ns |
| Shortest period that closes | 1.6 ns | 3.0 ns | 1.7 ns |
| Total power in `power.rpt`, 50 MHz | 52.6 µW | leakage only | 46.0 µW |
| Supply power at transistor level, 50 MHz | 57.2 µW | 779 µW | 55.7 µW |
| Static power at transistor level | 0.74 µW | 0.0036 µW | 1.70 µW |

ETH LV nearly halves the synthesised area, mostly because of the flip-flop without reset: IHP LV spends 56 µm² per bit on a flip-flop with an unused asynchronous reset plus its tie cell, ETH LV 23 µm². After place and route the gap narrows: timing repair adds hold buffers (20 `sg13g2_dlygate4sd3_1` with 327 µm² in IHP LV, 29 `BUFX3` with 164 µm² in ETH LV), and the tap cells of ETH LV follow the core and not the logic, which costs 436 µm² on this large, nearly empty die. IHP HV costs three times the area of IHP LV but needs no hold buffers.

In speed, the two thin-oxide libraries are close. At 20 ns the worst path starts at `enable_i` and runs through the hold buffers, so that slack says little about the library. The shortest period compares register-to-register paths, where IHP LV is slightly ahead. IHP HV closes at about 1.9 times that period.

The power numbers come with three caveats. First, on this nearly empty die the leakage is almost entirely decap fill (97 % in IHP LV and 99 % in ETH LV), which leaks more per area in ETH LV, while the logic of ETH LV alone leaks 12 nW against 22 nW in IHP LV. Second, the clock buffers decide more than the library: with `sg13g2_buf_4` and `BUFX12` as root buffer, the supply power drops to 37.2 µW for IHP LV and 29.4 µW for ETH LV, and the advantage of ETH LV grows from 2.5 % to 21 %. Third, the `power.rpt` numbers are vectorless estimates: they sit below the transistor-level values, more for ETH LV than for IHP LV, and for IHP HV the dynamic part is missing altogether. At 3.3 V, the supply power of IHP HV is 13.6 times that of IHP LV.
:::
